notes: expected.flaggedAnyOf: at least one claim element of one of these types must end up without support (a non-'supports' verdict, or listed as missing evidence). '*' means any element type other than 'product'. An empty list means nothing has to be flagged.
expected.citeAnyOf: at least one of these rule IDs must be cited (with a verified quote) in applicableRules or findings.
heldOut cases are not used while tuning the prompt and are reported separately.
stub cases replace the model with a scripted response, so they test the deterministic layer, not model judgment.

cases.rationale: A factual efficacy claim with no documentation. § 13 and 655/2013 3(1) require evidence; nothing contradicts the claim yet, so the next step is to request evidence.
Right product, outcome and method, but measurements stop at 12 hours. The 24-hour element is unsupported; a 24-hour study could still support it, so this is an evidence gap rather than a violation.
Controlled clinical study on the marketed formula (F-101 rev. 3) with a significant result at 24 hours.
The study tested development formula F-098, not the marketed F-101 rev. 3. Under 655/2013 3(3) studies must be relevant to the product; bridging evidence or a study on F-101 is needed.
Supplier data on the hyaluronic acid raw material, tested in vitro. It mentions 24 hours and hydration but says nothing about the finished product on people (655/2013 2(2), 3(6)).
Two studies on F-101 rev. 3 disagree at 24 hours. The weight of evidence (655/2013 3(7)) needs a reviewer's judgment; the claim cannot be cleared automatically.
The only study on this formula shows no significant effect at 24 hours, so the claim goes beyond the available evidence (655/2013 4(1)) and is likely misleading (§ 5).
The study shows -21 % at 4 weeks and -47 % only at 8 weeks. The claim combines the larger number with the shorter time, overstating the test results.

10 of 11 hand-picked existing customers agreeing in a questionnaire cannot support a general '9 out of 10 women' statement. A properly designed consumer test could, so this is an evidence gap. Some reviewers would call it a potential violation.

'Danmarks lækreste serum' and 'Forkæl din hud' are subjective praise that the average consumer does not take literally (655/2013 3(5)). Tests that the system does not demand evidence for everything. Some reviewers would still want a basis for the superlative.

cases.category: missing evidence (factual element inside sales language)
cases.rationale: Same sales language as the puffery case, plus 'vores bestseller', which is a verifiable factual statement (sales data) that must be documented under § 13.
Claims a cosmetic cures eczema and psoriasis. Anecdotes are not evidence, and the supplied evidence itself says no clinical studies exist. Bilag 1 nr. 17 (via § 9) and Art. 20(1) apply; escalate.
Truncated JSON must fail closed: manual review, never a clearance.

cases.category: invalid model response (unknown rule ID, invented quote)
cases.rationale: Schema-valid output that clears the claim while citing a rule ID that does not exist and a quote that is not in the evidence. The citation checks must downgrade it.

cases.category: invalid model response (clears using another formulation)
cases.rationale: Every quote is genuine, but the supporting study names formula F-098, not F-101 rev. 3. The deterministic identity check must block the clearance on its own.
